option.counterfactual: For every fixed graph H of chromatic number at least three satisfying ex(N,H)=t_r(N)+O(N), a graph maximizing both edges and cycles exists for every sufficiently large order, so every S_r is empty.
option.approach: Test the proposed universal statement on explicit forbidden graphs with known linear extremal corrections, such as odd wheels and friendship graphs. Calculate cycle comparisons among their competing extremal constructions to locate any obstruction to the statement.

judge.reason: It explicitly determines every set S_r as empty, which is the same claim as e1; empty sets have no finite boundary points.

options.counterfactual: The claimed simultaneous-extremizer theorem for all graphs satisfying ex(N,H)=t_r(N)+O(N) is false, and at least one set S_r is nonempty.
options.approach: Reassess the claimed theorem rather than use it as an established result. Identify precisely what hypotheses would be needed to guarantee a simultaneous edge-and-cycle maximizer.
